title: Chart generated from an HTML table
when: A page already has a data table, or the content belongs in a table, and the user wants a chart of it without duplicating the numbers.
prompt:
Goal: A script that reads a semantic table and renders a matching chart beside it, so the table stays the source and the fallback.
Steps:
1. Mark the table: <table data-chart="bar" data-series="2,3"> with <caption>, thead th headers and th scope="row" labels.
2. Read headers from thead textContent and values per tbody row, preferring a data-value attribute when the cell shows formatted text.
3. If any value is not finite or rows are missing, skip the chart; the table still works.
4. Render the chart named by data-chart with the shared chart functions, using the caption as its title.
5. Insert the chart before the table inside a <figure>, with a toggle button that hides only the visual view, never the table semantics.
6. Re-render on tbody changes (MutationObserver) and container resizes.
Quality bar:
- One source of truth: the table.
- Works on any table with the attributes.
- Without scripts the page shows the table alone.
Pitfalls:
- Parsing formatted numbers ("R$ 1.200") directly.
- Hiding the table with display none, losing the data for screen readers.
- Charting total rows together with their parts.
Verify:
- [ ] Table has caption and th headers.
- [ ] Numbers come from data-value or a locale parser.
- [ ] Chart title taken from the caption.
- [ ] Toggle button has type="button" and aria-pressed.
Output: js/table-chart.js enhancing every table[data-chart], plus the table markup.

examples.input: transformar a tabela de resultados do trimestre em gráfico
examples.output: table[data-chart=bar] read into bars above it, caption as title, Show table toggle
